title: Parrot Momentum Transfer Lab
description: A physics sandbox where a Parrot slides along frictionless rails at adjustable velocities and collides with a BoomBox on a flat surface. The user configures mass, velocity, and elasticity coefficients for both objects, launches collisions, and verifies conservation of momentum and kinetic energy. An undo/redo system lets the user step back through experiment configurations.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (importmap from cdn.jsdelivr.net) that implements a 1D collision lab. Load Parrot.glb (scaled to ~0.4) on the left and BoomBox.glb (scaled to 30) on the right, both resting on a visible flat platform (BoxGeometry, gray material). Use GLTFLoader from three/addons. Camera: PerspectiveCamera at (0,3,8) looking at origin. Add ambient light (0.6) and a directional light from (5,10,7). UI panel (HTML overlay, top-left): sliders for Parrot mass (0.5-5 kg), Parrot initial velocity (1-10 m/s), BoomBox mass (0.5-5 kg), BoomBox initial velocity (-5 to 0 m/s), and a restitution coefficient slider (0 for perfectly inelastic to 1 for perfectly elastic). Display live readouts of total momentum and total kinetic energy. Buttons: Launch, Reset, Undo, Redo. On Launch, animate the Parrot sliding right and BoomBox sliding left along the x-axis. On contact (bounding box overlap), compute post-collision velocities using the 1D elastic/inelastic collision formula with the chosen restitution. Animate both objects moving apart at computed velocities. Show a results overlay with pre- and post-collision momentum and KE, highlighting conservation. The Undo button reverts to the previous parameter configuration and positions (maintain a history stack of up to 20 states storing mass, velocity, restitution, and positions). Redo re-applies the undone state. Reset returns objects to starting positions with current slider values. Each Launch pushes current state onto the undo stack. The user must perform at least 10 interactions: adjust 5 sliders, launch twice with different settings, undo once, redo once, and reset once to fully explore the system. Use requestAnimationFrame for smooth animation and OrbitControls for camera rotation.
